`insight:india-mb-crisis-start` · confidence: verified

Of 28 windows in this library, 14 have their best starting point within about nine months of the Mar 2009 low (Bajaj Finance, Astral, Pidilite, Titan, Eicher, Balkrishna, APL Apollo, Deepak, Tata Elxsi, Avanti, Caplin, La Opala, Alkyl, Symphony). Another nine start within about six months of the Mar 2020 COVID low (KPIT, Trent, Cochin, Mazagon, HAL, BEL, BSE, Suzlon, and CDSL near it). Only Page (2007 IPO), Garware (2013), Polycab/Dixon (2019 IPO/low) and Kaynes (2022 IPO) start elsewhere. Two implications. (1) The headline multiples (100–2,000x) are partly a start-point artefact; buying the same names a year before or after the crash gives 2–5x less. (2) The real edge was owning or buying quality growers when they were at 5–15x during a panic; in 2008–09 and 2020 many of these traded at single-digit P/E. Process: keep a ready list of high-ROCE, low-debt compounders with pre-set 'crash prices' so a crash is an execution step, not a decision. Survival (no leverage, cash reserve) is what makes this possible. Link: insight:avoid-ruin.

Links: `insight:avoid-ruin` (about), `insight:behavior-gap` (about), `strategy:position-sizing` (about)

body:
- Blinkit moved to an inventory-led model in FY26. Revenue went from 20,243 to **54,364 (+169%)**, but management reported like-for-like growth at a fraction of that (see Lesson 3.3).
- The working-capital profile flipped. Payable days fell from 101 to 36, CCC went from −54 days to +2, and FCF went from −623 to −1,114.
- **Lesson:** when the revenue definition changes, recompute every per-revenue ratio (margins, DSO, asset turnover) on a like-for-like basis.

title: course › 2.4 Business-model change (gross-up) and working capital: Eternal (ETERNAL)

body:
1. CWIP share = 400/1,000 = **40%**. Aged >3y share = 250/400 = **62.5%**. Capitalised interest / total finance cost = 45/(30 + 45) = **60%**. That is three flags. True finance cost is 2.5x what the P&L shows, and a "project" older than 3 years is a candidate for impairment. Verdict: **disqualifying until explained**. Ask for the project's name, budget, COD date and the auditor's comment.
2. Incremental D&A + interest = (3,974 − 760) + (1,902 − 563) = 3,214 + 1,339 = 4,553. Pre-116 EBITDA ≈ 4,090 − 4,553 = **−463**, against FY19's −149. The business deteriorated, while reported EBITDA swung from −149 to +4,090. (Approximation: lease additions and fleet growth also matter.)
3. Tax demands: haircut by historical settlement rates, then read the nature of the disputes. Perhaps 10–30% is at risk, so treat it as a cash-risk footnote. Guarantees for promoter-group companies: add **₹900 cr to debt**. That is 45% of net worth, a related-party governance flag (flag #8) and a sign that group stress can transmit to this company.

`insight:flag-high-roe-context` · verified

RULE: a high ROE is a result to be explained, not a quality. Decompose it (DuPont: margin x asset turn x leverage) and ask which leg carries it. SUSPECT WHEN: (1) CFO is far below PAT for several years in a non-lender (profits not becoming cash); (2) ROE comes from leverage (equity a thin slice; NBFC leverage >7-8x; DHFL ~10x); (3) in a lender, ROE is lifted by low provisions on a fast-growing book: new loans have not had time to default (Yes Bank FY18: ROE 17.7%, GNPA 1.28%, loans +54%, while RBI's divergence reports showed NPAs under-recognised by Rs 4,177 cr in FY16 and Rs 6,355 cr in FY17); (4) margins/ROCE far above peers in a commodity-like business with no visible mechanism (Vakrangee ROCE ~40% in rural kiosks); (5) ROE flattered by buybacks or a shrinking equity base from write-offs. BENIGN WHEN: ROE comes from high margins or asset turns with low debt and is matched by CFO (Page 45-69% ROCE, Pidilite, APL Apollo at 5-8% margins but ~0 WC days), or in a bank from low-cost deposits, granular seasoned retail loans and stable credit costs (HDFC Bank 16-20% for a decade). TEST: 5-year CFO/PAT; leverage; for lenders: loan growth vs system (>2-3x system = red), lagged NPA (NPA / loans of 2-3 years ago), divergence notes, CASA, top-20 exposures; compare ROE with the best peer and ask why it is higher.

body:
- **id:** `thesis:paper-call:HDFCLIFE:fy27-vnb-growth-12pct-plus`
- **Method:** management-tone-vs-delivery · **P(ours)** 0.52 · **P(base)** 0.45 · resolve by 2027-05-15
- **Evidence:** H1 FY27 call (15-Oct-2026): H1 VNB ₹2,037 cr (+12%), Q2 VNB +15%; new-business margin 24.7% (H1 FY26 24.5%); individual APE +9% H1, total APE +11% H1 / +13% Q2; HDFC Bank channel APE +12% in Q2 ('growth momentum coming back'). MD: 'momentum is building… VNB growth ahead of APE'; GST impact 'now gets baked into the business model from second half'. Headwinds: H2 FY26 protection grew 57% (base effect), ULIP persistency softer, IRDAI consultation papers on distribution economics. FY26 (Q4 FY26 call, Apr-2026): VNB ₹4,034 cr (+2%), margin 24.2% (25.5% ex GST/SSV).
- **Why our number differs from base:** Management tone is the most upbeat in two years and the GST drag on margins laps in H2, so H2 VNB growth ≥12% is plausible; but the 57% protection base and IRDAI commission rules are real. Tone slightly ahead of what H1 numbers alone imply; we are a bit above base.
- **Base-rate reasoning:** Naive: a life insurer's full-year VNB growth lands at or above its H1 growth rate a bit under half the time (H2 is the larger half and often slower).
- **Resolution rule:** YES if HDFC Life's reported FY27 VNB ÷ FY26 VNB (₹4,034 cr, or FY26 as restated in the Q4 FY27 deck) − 1 ≥ 12.0%, using the company's stated growth if given.
- **Resolution source:** HDFC Life Q4 FY27 investor presentation / earnings call (NSE)
- **Sources used:** https://nsearchives.nseindia.in/corporate/HDFCLIFE2_23102026153545_SE_Transcript.pdf; https://nsearchives.nseindia.in/corporate/PRASAD_23042026224833_EarningsCallTranscript.pdf
- **Confidence of evidence:** verified
